partners.diseaseBName: familial hyperthyroidism due to mutations in TSH receptor
partners.mechanism_chain: LHB (HGNC:6677) —DECREASES→ Glycoprotein synthesis (GO:0009100); Glycoprotein synthesis (GO:0009100) —LEADS_TO→ Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (MONDO:0009223); TSHR (HGNC:11956) —INCREASES→ Thyroid hormone synthesis (GO:0007307); Thyroid hormone synthesis (GO:0007307) —LEADS_TO→ Familial hyperthyroidism (MONDO:0012203); Glycoprotein synthesis (GO:0009100) —BINDS→ Thyroid hormone synthesis (GO:0007307). Loss of function in LHB leads to reduced gonadotropin signaling, impacting glycoprotein synthesis, which in turn affects downstream pathways including thyroid hormone synthesis, contributing to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Conversely, gain-of-function mutations in TSHR lead to overactive thyroid hormone synthesis, causing familial hyperthyroidism. The convergence is proposed at the level of shared pathways, specifically glycoprotein synthesis which is essential for both hormonal signaling and thyroid hormone production.

#### 1. congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-193993)

**Proposed mechanism:** LHB (HGNC:6627) —DISRUPTS→ Luteinizing hormone signaling (REACT:R-HSA-166080); Luteinizing hormone signaling (REACT:R-HSA-166080) —LEADS_TO→ Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HP:0000037); HSD3B2 (HGNC:4918) —DISRUPTS→ Steroidogenesis (REACT:R-HSA-150405); Steroidogenesis (REACT:R-HSA-150405) —DECREASES→ Androgens (CHEBI:23912); Androgens (CHEBI:23912) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (HP:0000199); Steroidogenesis (REACT:R-HSA-150405) —LEADS_TO→ Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HP:0000037). Loss-of-function mutations in LHB disrupt luteinizing hormone signaling, leading to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Separately, loss-of-function mutations in HSD3B2 disrupt steroidogenesis, leading to reduced androgen production and congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Both diseases converge on the downstream consequences of disrupted steroid hormone production and signaling, impacting reproductive and adrenal function respectively.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in LHB in individuals diagnosed with congenital adrenal hyperplasia, or pathogenic variants in HSD3B2 in individuals diagnosed with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, without a clear secondary explanation, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 for the specific pathogenic variants in LHB or HSD3B2 in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of steroidogenesis in these distinct conditions could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting hormone replacement or pathway modulation for improved patient outcomes. For example, insights into the HSD3B2 deficiency could inform management of gonadal dysfunction in CAH patients, and conversely, understanding the role of LH signaling in steroidogenesis could offer new avenues for treating hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
